- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap next 3-day forecast at +3% above peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.2), model underestimates upward momentum; add 2–4% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action; weight recent 7-day history 3x more than older data.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.3), model delays reaction; add 1–2 days lag to forecast adjustment.
- If 30-day forecast mean is below 75, and sentiment is negative, add 3–5% upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings >0.4, increase forecast standard deviation by 15–20%.
